claims.text: Claude autonomously designed protein binders against 16 targets, with binders confirmed for 14 of the 15 targets with interpretable data.
claims.citation: Anthropic technical report: 'Claude obtained binders against 14 of the 15 targets'

claims.text: 354 of 1,320 designs bound their targets, a hit rate of 26.8% by the integrated call.
claims.citation: Anthropic technical report: '354 of the 1,320 designs bound their targets, a hit rate of 26.8%'; Adaptyv: '354 of all designs (1,320) bound their target, an overall hit rate of 26.8%'

claims.text: Per-target hit rates ranged from 0% (MBP, 0/90) to 80% (TREM2, 72/90).
claims.citation: Anthropic technical report: '72 binders out of 90 designs on TREM2 ... 0 of 90 on MBP'

claims.text: The 26.8% figure is an orchestration result from ten open-source structure-generation methods, not a single-model design.
claims.citation: Anthropic technical report Methods: released per-design provenance lists PXDesign, RFdiffusion3, Genie 3, FreeBindCraft, BindCraft, BoltzGen, RFdiffusion, Proteina-Complexa, FoldCraft, BoltzDesign1, Protein Hunter

claims.text: RFdiffusion (Nature 2023) reported a 19% overall experimental binder success rate, roughly two orders of magnitude above prior Rosetta methods.
claims.citation: Watson et al. Nature 2023: 'The overall experimental success rate ... was 19%'; Fig 6b caption: prior estimated success rates 0%–5.5%

claims.text: Anthropic's blog compares against a '10-15% typical' figure and Adaptyv competitions, not RFdiffusion's 19%.
claims.citation: Anthropic blog: 'compared to the 10-15% that is typical in protein design campaigns today'; competition comparisons in the technical report

claims.text: A direct 26.8% versus 19% comparison is not a controlled benchmark due to differing targets, assays, budgets and generator eras.
claims.citation: Inference from RFdiffusion Nature 2023 methods (10 uM single-point BLI) vs Anthropic technical report (two-CRO integrated call)

claims.text: Mythos Preview hit 26.7% (104/390) and Opus 4.8 22.6% (88/390) in multi-target mode; Mythos single-target 35.1% (158/450); top-ranked design bound 49% of the time.
claims.citation: Anthropic technical report Results: 'Opus 4.8 produced 88 binders from 390 designs (22.6%) and Mythos Preview produced 104 from 390 (26.7%)'; 'Mythos Preview produced 158 binders from 450 designs (35.1%)'; 'the hit rate was 49% for the top-ranked design alone'

claims.text: On RBX1, 28 of 90 Claude designs bound versus 9 of 245 in the open competition; tightest 3.9 nM vs winner's 45 nM re-measured on the same plate.
claims.citation: Anthropic technical report: 'RBX1 (28/90 against 9/245)'; 'bound free RBX1 at 3.9 nM ... the competition winner bound at 45 nM'

claims.text: Claude designed 12 TNFalpha binders (8%), all from Opus 4.8, on a target where other de novo efforts reported none.
claims.citation: Anthropic technical report: 'Twelve of Claude's 150 TNFalpha designs bound (8.0% hit rate), all of them designed by Opus 4.8'; discussion notes prior reports of none [5,7,14]

claims.text: On novel targets 15-PGDH and latent GDF-8, Claude scored 1/30 and 14/60, comparable to or better than competition fields (1/106 and 6/100).
claims.citation: Anthropic technical report: '15-PGDH (1/30 against 1/106)'; 'latent GDF-8 (14/60 against 6/100)'

claims.text: The integrated-call binder definition broadened the count above Adaptyv's own classification (roughly 336 of 1,296).
claims.citation: Anthropic technical report Methods: 'Adaptyv Bio returned a result for 1,296 ... (336 binders ...)'; 'added 19 that it had not'

claims.text: The report disclaims that Claude's designs are better than an expert with the same tools and budget, and describes campaigns rather than models.
claims.citation: Anthropic technical report Discussion: 'we do not claim that Claude's designs are better than an expert would obtain with the same tools and budget'; 'we have described campaigns rather than models'

claims.text: ProteinBase and Overath corpus: roughly 770 binders out of 5,700 designs against 40 targets; Overath analyzed 3,766 binders across 15 targets.
claims.citation: Anthropic blog: 'approximately 770 binders out of 5,700 designs against 40 targets'; Overath et al. bioRxiv abstract: '3,766 experimentally tested binders across 15 structurally diverse targets'

claims.text: Every model Claude used was open-source; Anthropic releases prompts, models and both CROs' data under CC BY 4.0.
claims.citation: Anthropic technical report: 'Every design and prediction model available to Claude was open-source'; 'released ... under CC BY 4.0'
